requirements.statement: When the `--json` option is given, the tool MUST print the counts of lines, words and characters as one JSON object with the keys lines, words and characters, in that order.
When the `--json` option is not given, the tool MUST print exactly what it printed before this change, byte for byte.
When the input cannot be read, the tool MUST print nothing on standard output, write a message on standard error and exit with status 1, whether or not the `--json` option is given.
The JSON object MUST be followed by a single line break and MUST hold no other text.

risks.description: a script may read the keys in a different order than the tool prints them, so the order is part of the contract

specification.summary: A person who writes scripts runs the tool with the `--json` option and gets the three counts as one JSON object, so another program can read them without parsing columns of text.
